capabilities: Run fenced code blocks in 17 languages with a run button and inline output
Provide stdin input interactively (desktop Python) or pre-filled via a form
Wrap incomplete code snippets in a language-appropriate program skeleton before running
Cache output across note switches and render ANSI colors and compiler diagnostics
Expose a plugin API so other plugins can execute code blocks programmatically
extras: Pending community-plugin approval; manual installation described. Twelve of the seventeen languages run on remote playground APIs (20 s timeout) and require internet; Python and JS/TS/HTML/Wenyan run locally, with Python needing a ~10 MB Pyodide download on first run.
intentEvidence: Forked from Code Emitter by YISH (MIT). Key additions:
problem: Obsidian renders code blocks as inert text, so code in notes (especially short lecture-note fragments) cannot be executed or tested in place.
